title: Slow walking and ageing
paragraphs: Getting old might not be something that’s yet to cross your mind. But ageing is inevitably going to get the better of us one day, so it’s something I’m sure we’d all like control. It would be great to have a long, healthy and happy life, and that’s why scientists are constantly seeking out evidence that will show us what we need to do to achieve longevity.

We all know that regular exercise is good for us. In recent years we’ve been told to aim to walk 10,000 steps a day to remain healthy, although other advice to do three brisk 10-minute walks a day is thought to be even more effective. But the latest piece of research might put a spring in your step if you’re someone who walks at a fast pace. That’s because, according to scientists, the speed at which people walk in their 40s is a sign of how much their brains, as well as their bodies, are ageing.

The BBC’s Philippa Roxby writes that tests on 1,000 people from New Zealand born in the 1970s found that slower walkers tended to show signs of "accelerated ageing". Their lungs, teeth and immune systems were in worse shape than those who walked faster. And to add insult to injury, the study found not only did slower walkers' bodies age more quickly, their faces looked older and they had smaller brains. Professor Terrie E Moffitt, lead author of the study, told the BBC: "[it] found that a slow walk is a problem sign decades before old age."

This might be seen as a wake-up call for people with a slower gait who might feel it’s time to work out and get fitter. But it might be too late; researchers writing in JAMA Network Open say they were able to predict the walking speed of 45-year-olds using the results of intelligence, language and motor skills tests from when they were aged three. They also suggest that even in early life, there are signs showing which people will go on to have a healthier life.

So, what’s the point of knowing that a slower walking pace might mean a smaller brain? Well, researchers say measuring walking speed at a younger age, and understanding what this might mean, could be a way of testing treatments to slow human ageing. This might help us make lifestyle changes while we’re still young and healthy. Any steps we can take to prolong a good mental and physical state is a no brainer!

vocabulary.entry: ageing /ˈeɪdʒɪŋ/ n. 衰老；老化
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can slow down the ageing process.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动能延缓衰老过程。

vocabulary.entry: inevitably /ɪnˈevɪtəbli/ adv. 不可避免地；必然地
vocabulary.example: Technology will inevitably change the way we work.
vocabulary.translation: 技术必然会改变我们的工作方式。

vocabulary.entry: get the better of /ɡet ðə ˈbetə(r) ɒv/ 战胜；压倒
vocabulary.example: Don’t let fear get the better of you.
vocabulary.translation: 别让恐惧战胜你。

vocabulary.entry: longevity /lɒnˈdʒevəti/ n. 长寿；寿命
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet is key to longevity.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡饮食是长寿的关键。

vocabulary.entry: regular exercise /ˈreɡjələ(r) ˈeksəsaɪz/ 规律运动
vocabulary.example: She maintains her fitness through regular exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 她通过规律运动保持健康。

vocabulary.entry: brisk walk /brɪsk wɔːk/ 快走；快步走
vocabulary.example: A brisk walk for 20 minutes a day is good for the heart.
vocabulary.translation: 每天快走20分钟对心脏有益。

vocabulary.term: put a spring in your step
vocabulary.entry: put a spring in your step /pʊt ə sprɪŋ ɪn jɔː(r) step/ 让你步伐轻快；使你干劲十足
vocabulary.example: The good news put a spring in her step.
vocabulary.translation: 这个好消息让她干劲十足。

vocabulary.entry: accelerated ageing /əkˈseləreɪtɪd ˈeɪdʒɪŋ/ 加速衰老
vocabulary.example: Poor sleep quality can lead to accelerated ageing.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠质量差会导致加速衰老。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˈsɪstəm/ 免疫系统
vocabulary.example: Vitamin C helps boost the immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 维生素C有助于增强免疫系统。

vocabulary.entry: in worse shape /ɪn wɜːs ʃeɪp/ 状况更差
vocabulary.example: His knee is in worse shape than before the treatment.
vocabulary.translation: 他的膝盖状况比治疗前更糟了。

vocabulary.entry: add insult to injury /æd ˈɪnsʌlt tu ˈɪndʒəri/ 雪上加霜；更糟的是
vocabulary.example: First he missed the bus, then to add insult to injury, it started raining.
vocabulary.translation: 他先是没赶上公交车，更糟的是，天还下起了雨。

vocabulary.entry: wake-up call /ˈweɪk ʌp kɔːl/ 警钟；警示
vocabulary.example: The accident was a wake-up call for better safety measures.
vocabulary.translation: 这场事故为加强安全措施敲响了警钟。

vocabulary.entry: gait /ɡeɪt/ n. 步态；走路姿势
vocabulary.example: The doctor noticed a slight limp in her gait.
vocabulary.translation: 医生注意到她走路有点跛。

vocabulary.entry: work out /wɜːk aʊt/ 锻炼身体；健身
vocabulary.example: I work out at the gym three times a week.
vocabulary.translation: 我每周去健身房锻炼三次。

vocabulary.entry: motor skills /ˈməʊtə(r) skɪlz/ 运动技能
vocabulary.example: Children develop motor skills through play.
vocabulary.translation: 儿童通过玩耍发展运动技能。

vocabulary.entry: predict /prɪˈdɪkt/ v. 预测；预言
vocabulary.example: Experts predict a rise in temperatures next month.
vocabulary.translation: 专家预测下个月气温会上升。

vocabulary.entry: treatment /ˈtriːtmənt/ n. 疗法；治疗
vocabulary.example: The new treatment has shown promising results.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新疗法已显示出良好的效果。

vocabulary.entry: lifestyle changes /ˈlaɪfstaɪl ˈtʃeɪndʒɪz/ 生活方式的改变
vocabulary.example: 改变生活方式有助于缓解压力。
vocabulary.translation: Lifestyle changes can help manage stress.

vocabulary.entry: prolong /prəˈlɒŋ/ v. 延长；拉长
vocabulary.example: Medication can prolong the patient’s life.
vocabulary.translation: 药物能延长病人的生命。

vocabulary.translation: 瑜伽有助于改善身心健康状态。

vocabulary.entry: no brainer /nəʊ ˈbreɪnə(r)/ 显而易见的事；无需思考的决定
vocabulary.example: Accepting the job offer was a no brainer for her.
vocabulary.translation: 接受这份工作对她来说是显而易见的明智选择。

vocabulary.entry: seek out /siːk aʊt/ 寻找；找出
vocabulary.example: She sought out advice from a financial expert.
vocabulary.translation: 她向金融专家寻求建议。
